propositions: CLI write-command argument parsing currently uses hand-rolled loops with bespoke semantics that diverge from observable behavior (e.g., --assignee absent vs. empty string sentinel); refactor to stdlib argparse without changing CLI behavior

argparse refactor must preserve command-specific --force semantics: claim bare --force consumes next non-option token or defaults to '(no reason given)'; transition bare --force sets force_reason='' (not None) and does NOT consume following tokens
--assignee must preserve None-vs-empty-string distinction (absent → None → default_assignee fallback; explicit empty string → cleared assignee)

transition._parse_flags is retained as an argparse-backed shim returning identical 5-tuple to support three external direct callers (test_close_ref_target_80af.py, test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py, test_dependency_audit.py) without changes
--help is dispatcher-served byte-exact from golden help files (help/claim.txt, help/transition.txt); argparse parser does NOT generate help

Unknown tokens silently skipped via parse_known_args; allow_abbrev=False disables prefix matching; retired --force-close rejected with exit-1; value-less flags exit 1 with existing error messages (not argparse's exit-2)
